prior_public_neighbors.decisive_difference: B1n classifies entanglement after a rotation and controlled NOT. H1 rephases a Hermitian decomposition. C1s computes the input table required to commute two gates and locates the angles at which an unchanged table passes.

decisive_difference: The intermediate label changes which phase multiplies each column. The task demands a necessary and sufficient global test for leaving an arbitrary table in place, an exact two-bit calibration for all angles, and a superposition witnessing the failure of the uncorrected order. A phase-free permutation product alone cannot supply those results.
admission_decision: Propose an uncounted D2 starting item within the shared C1s–C3s study family. Preserve the pullback and relative-phase exposure links across any future split. The comparisons cover the resolved 198 retained contracts, the 15 historical reservations, 18 workbook entries, public assessment family records and pilot, and all 7 plus 6 questions in the two preceding public deliveries.
full_credit_work: Act on one basis ket to obtain weight \(a(x)b(p(x))\) and label \(q(p(x))\). Identify \(g=f\circ p\) and prove uniqueness. Give both directions of the exact orbit-invariance test and the single-constant test for \(f(p(x))/f(x)\), with a fixed sign convention for that constant. On two bits compute the table \(e^{i\theta(t\oplus c)}\), use the fixed control-zero columns to fix any common phase, and use a moved column to identify all angles. At \(\theta=\pi\) propagate a normalized two-term input through both orders, establish orthogonality, and explain equality of the basis-input output probabilities.

prior_public_neighbors.shared_subproof: Both packets model a permutation route by a complex number attached to its input column, and W2 compares phases on colliding routes.
prior_public_neighbors.decisive_difference: W1 and W2 combine different routes into a clean matrix entry and optimize or certify a budget. C2s compares two devices on the same labeled route by constructing a single diagonal change of basis compatible with prescribed reference values.

prior_public_neighbors.shared_subproof: H1 follows rephasing explicitly, H2 checks compatibility of independently supplied data, and B2n diagnoses underdetermined complex data.
prior_public_neighbors.decisive_difference: C2s constrains a phase at every directed edge by the reference phases at its two ends. The coupled conditions run along orbit arcs and close around a cycle. The prior tasks use one common scalar, Pauli-block consistency and measurement of a single coherence, respectively.

shared_subproof: Plan313 classifies plain permutations under relabeling. BE108 and LA013 explicitly conjugate under a basis permutation, while BE111 fixes chronological order. BE104 and LA016 distinguish an overall phase from exact matrix equality. The reserved Plan305 concerns tensor-factor permutation conjugation and its coefficients. Workbook C2 cancels neighboring gauges on a tensor train with fixed endpoints, B2 corrects relative phases in one output, and B4 uses a fixed relabeling. Cycle closure and consistency of several external phase references are new obligations here.
decisive_difference: The allowed conjugation is diagonal and labels stay fixed. An unconstrained match requires one oriented product per cycle. Prescribed phases add constraints along arcs in that cycle, and the construction must recover every calibrating diagonal including its componentwise freedom. Two prescribed phases can obstruct an otherwise valid match.
admission_decision: Propose an uncounted D3 transfer item in the same exposure family as C1s and C3s. The graph anchors establish weighted basis action and composition. The labeled-cycle classification and fixed-reference extension are authored deductions. Comparison covers the 198 retained contracts, 15 historical reservations, 18 workbook entries, public assessment family records and pilot, and all 7 plus 6 questions in the preceding deliveries.
full_credit_work: Derive the edge equation \(d_{p(x)}=(b_x/a_x)d_x\). Prove full-cycle consistency and compatibility of reference ratios with products of \(b_x/a_x\) along forward arcs. Show the cycle products classify an unpinned labeled cycle under diagonal conjugation, construct the phases from a base choice for each cycle, and show that every solution is obtained. An unpinned cycle has one free unit scalar, and a compatible pinned cycle has none. Include one reference, several references and fixed points. Construct two candidate devices with equal cycle products but inconsistent prescribed endpoints on a single cycle, and identify the specific failing arc.

proposed_use: Public study/proposed-training candidate. Official split unassigned.
family_group: Monomial unitaries on labeled permutation cycles
assessment_overlap: The public v2 permutation_heisenberg_pullback family transports a quantity under a basis permutation, and internal_bond_phase_interference concerns coherent phase information lost by some observations. The v3 public extension adds promise_register_protocols. The controlled_permutation_semantics pilot studies phase-free products and inverses. Our repeated powers use the composition substrate, but the observations here are complex traces of a known routing pattern with unknown edge phases.

prior_public_neighbors.shared_subproof: Complex routes can give ambiguous aggregate observations. W1 distinguishes the aggregate clean entry from its per-slot values, and W2 checks when a column sum reveals a full cap budget.
prior_public_neighbors.decisive_difference: C3s deals with characteristic factors of repeated orbits and power traces of a single unitary, then recovers products through divisibility or from measurements resolved by cycle length. The six-label ambiguity even preserves the full spectrum.

prior_public_neighbors.shared_subproof: H3 uses observations resolved by auxiliary eigenspace, B2n reconstructs a complex parameter from measurements, and B3n asks what observables leave undetermined.
prior_public_neighbors.decisive_difference: C3s derives an inverse problem for traces of powers. It must detect a polynomial collision across cycle lengths, invert a triangular system for distinct lengths, and recover repeated roots from sector power sums. Neither an affine Hamiltonian fit nor parity-state tomography supplies these steps.

shared_subproof: Plan108 uses trace invariance, Plan109 recovers representation multiplicities from a full character, and Plan313 groups unweighted permutations by cycle length. Plan415 estimates a density spectrum with symmetry restrictions. BE111 and BE110 implement phase-free routes. Reserved Plan219 distinguishes taking ordinary powers from transforming singular values. Workbook P1 uses a particular eigenvector of a cyclic shift; B2 distinguishes relative phases through coherent readout; C3 computes inner-product data through a recurrence. None of those recovery problems assigns independent edge products to labeled cycles from powers of one unknown matrix.
decisive_difference: The data aggregate all lengths in each power. Distinct cycle lengths admit recursive labeled recovery even with divisibility. Repeated lengths can even conceal changes to the multiset at a given length. Length-resolved reports recover each multiset with multiplicity, while any unequal products within a length still allow assignments to different labels.
admission_decision: Propose an uncounted D4 transfer item and keep the C1s–C3s family linked for exposure. The cycle trace formula, spectral factorization and inverse problems are authored deductions from the weighted composition law. Comparison covers 198 retained contracts, 15 historical reservations, 18 workbook entries, public assessment family records and pilot, and all 7 plus 6 preceding public questions.
full_credit_work: Iterate the basis action and separate fixed labels of a power from nonreturning labels. Show that a length-\(\ell\) orbit contributes \(z^\ell-h_C\) to \(\det(zI-U)\) and contributes \(\ell h_C^{n/\ell}\) to \(t_n\) only when \(\ell\mid n\). For distinct lengths recover the product on the unique length-\(\ell\) cycle from \(t_\ell\) after subtracting all shorter divisor contributions, including the base case. With two fixed points and two transpositions, realize two assignments by unit phases and verify a common characteristic polynomial or equality of every trace, together with different within-length multisets. For the augmented observations, divide length-resolved traces by \(\ell\), use the first \(m_\ell\) power sums to reconstruct the monic polynomial of cycle products and all root multiplicities. Show that within-length permutations of products leave the reports invariant, and characterize unique labeled assignment for each length, including the cases of one cycle or identical products.
